description: Is valid UTF-8 (RFC 3629) encoded JSON per RFC 8259, with no leading byte-order mark and no object holding two members whose names are equal (§5). Note: parsers differ on repeated names and on a leading byte-order mark, so the same bytes could yield different values; excluding both follows RFC 8259 §8.1, which forbids adding a byte-order mark, and interoperable-JSON practice (RFC 7493 §2.3).
notes: Inline documents cover ordinary parsed values; documentText preserves duplicate keys and malformed JSON; documentBase64 carries exact bytes for invalid UTF-8 and a forbidden leading byte-order mark. Runners must hand the selected carriage to the strict document parser without pre-normalizing it.

tests.description: minimal valid OBI document
OBI document exercising several JSON value types
duplicate root object key is invalid even when both values are individually valid
duplicate key nested inside an operation object is invalid
leading UTF-8 byte-order mark is forbidden
a text holding an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence is not UTF-8 encoded JSON
malformed JSON text is invalid

a leading byte-order mark makes the text non-conformant through OBI-01 alone: OBI-02 to OBI-13 apply only to the JSON value of a text that meets OBI-01, so the dependency on a missing operation violates no other rule (section 10)
a repeated operations member makes the text non-conformant through OBI-01 alone, whichever value a parser keeps: OBI-02 to OBI-13 apply only to the JSON value of a text that meets OBI-01 (section 10)
a NaN literal is not a JSON value (RFC 8259 section 6), so the text is malformed JSON
a comma after the last member of an object is malformed JSON (RFC 8259 section 4)
a key written with an escape repeats the same key written plainly: member names are compared after unescaping (RFC 8259 section 8.3, section 5)
an ill-formed byte in another member's string means the text is not UTF-8, so it declares no version, these rules govern it (section 8.1, Version declaration), and it is non-conformant
a text with a leading byte-order mark declares no version, so these rules govern it, whatever version its openbindings member holds (section 8.1)
UTF-16 text without a byte-order mark declares no version, since its zero bytes break the JSON grammar
an ill-formed byte inside the openbindings value means the text is not UTF-8, so it declares no version
an ill-formed byte within an escape means the text is not UTF-8, so it declares no version
an ill-formed byte between tokens means the text is not UTF-8, so it declares no version
an ill-formed byte in the openbindings member's name means the text is not UTF-8, so it declares no version
a text with a repeated openbindings member declares no version, whatever its values, so these rules govern it (section 8.1)
A text with an ill-formed UTF-8 byte declares no version, even when its openbindings member reads another line, so these rules govern it (section 8.1)
openbindings and an escaped \u006fpenbindings are one name repeated, so the text declares no version and violates OBI-01 (section 8.1, Version declaration)
